original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read Model section 1 of the three-register bound and identify the exact excluded free operations.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks whether a larger or nonabelian register model escapes the scoped three-register obstruction. This package proves a different identity: every diagonal over every F2-algebra has exact minimum t when right vectors are F2-valued. The three-register rational model and the chain-ring hypothesis are not the alphabets under test.
actual_scope: Exact diagonal minimum for I+u y^T with y in F2^n over an arbitrary F2-algebra, plus the finite-group label corollary and a ring-valued right-vector sharpness witness.
bottleneck_link: A legal diagonal shorter than t would be a new bit primitive in every group algebra. The F2-span bound shows this alphabet does not supply one; kappa is unchanged.
stop_rule: Prove the F2-column bound and the coordinate construction, separate it from the chain-ring and torsion-free notes on the pin, check the sharpness witness with a second multiplier, exhaust the Klein and S3 controls, then stop.
evidence: PROOF.md is the uniform argument. verify.py compares two Klein multiplications, exhausts 1049600 Klein words and 19740 S3 words, and checks the ring-valued witness. RESULT.json is compared, not regenerated, by the default command.
author: Wentao Li
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance for the column argument, independent finite checks, and package metadata.

open_questions.question: Do free GL_n(F2) changes of basis between paid factors realize a diagonal with fewer than t factors?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The column argument evaluates P-I on the standard basis. A free basis change can move the endpoint out of that coordinate frame.
open_questions.first_step: Enumerate n=2 with every change of basis and a single paid factor, and record whether any diagonal with t=2 appears.
open_questions.blocked_by: No invariant for the conjugated endpoint is proved here. Do not replace that step with an order-at-most-16 group-label search.

open_questions.question: What native frame, hosting, and precision bill does one legal coordinate word pay?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The exact call count is not a supplier invoice, so it does not move a physical tariff.
open_questions.first_step: Price one coordinate word on an existing supplier meter without changing the alphabet.
open_questions.blocked_by: This note has no physical schedule and does not change kappa.

overlap.not_a_corollary_because: The chain-ring product theorem assumes R=F2[z]/(z^q) and R-valued right vectors. Its own Klein socle witness shows the column lemma fails off that hypothesis, and the displayed ring-valued outer product realizes t=2 in one factor. The F2-valued count is the complementary statement.
